title: Quantum Reference Frames in terms of Tetrads
authors: Jeremy Butterfield, Daniel A. Turolla Vanzella
abstract: We adapt to the context of quantum theory the treatment, familiar in relativity theory, of a reference frame as a tetrad. Since a tetrad is a set of four orthonormal vectors at a spacetime point, it encodes a timelike direction, three orthogonal spatial directions, and units; and so it gives a configuration in spacetime (a spatial orientation and state of motion) of an idealized infinitesimal apparatus (``rulers and a clock"). So a natural ``first guess" is that the state of a quantum reference frame should be an assignment of complex amplitudes to a set of tetrads. We develop this idea, in terms of bundles over spacetime of bases of the tangent spaces.   This paper is a companion to two other papers. It emphasises the main conceptual aspects of our proposal, while the other two papers give physical details. It also explains the main contrast between those two papers. Namely: (i) the first considers a single spacetime geometry, so that a quantum reference frame, on our proposal, gives a superposition of perspectives on that geometry; while (ii) the second considers the spacetime manifold with no geometry given a priori, which will imply that a quantum reference frame, on our proposal, can describe a superposition of perspectives on a superposition of geometries---not ``just" a superposition of perspectives on a single geometry. The main mathematical idea for representing this contrast will be choosing between (i) the orthonormal frame bundle, for a given spacetime geometry; (ii) the frame bundle in the usual sense of containing all bases of all spacetime points' tangent spaces.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework for Quantum Reference Frames (QRFs) by treating the reference frame itself as a quantum object defined over the space of tetrads. It uses fibre bundle theory to distinguish between scenarios where the QRF superposes perspectives on one geometry versus superposing over multiple possible geometries. The work culminates in deriving a unique, invariant volume element on the general frame bundle.
main_problem: The paper adapts the relativistic concept of a reference frame as a tetrad to the quantum domain, formalizing the state of a Quantum Reference Frame (QRF). It aims to distinguish between superpositions of perspectives on a single geometry versus superpositions of geometries themselves.
main_result: The formalism is constructed using the language of fibre bundles, distinguishing between the orthonormal frame bundle (for fixed geometry) and the general frame bundle (for variable geometry). The construction yields a unique, invariant volume element on the general frame bundle.
method: The authors use differential geometry, specifically analyzing the structure and invariance of volume elements on the frame bundle $F(M)$ by stipulating that the basis field acts as a tetrad field.
model_or_system: The system is the Quantum Reference Frame (QRF), whose state is proposed to be a complex amplitude assignment over the space of tetrads. The mathematical framework is built upon fibre bundles over spacetime, specifically the frame bundle $F(M)$.
key_observables: The state of the QRF, which is a complex function on the relevant set of tetrads, and the expectation values of observables derived from coupling the QRF to measured systems.
important_parameters: The choice between the orthonormal frame bundle (restricted QRF) and the general frame bundle (general QRF) dictates the physical interpretation of the superposition.
main_assumptions: The core assumptions involve treating the reference frame via tetrads, and mathematically, the determination of the invariant volume element relies on stipulating orthonormality (a tetrad condition) to fix the constant in the Haar measure.
paper_structure: The paper is structured conceptually, outlining the proposal's scope by contrasting the restricted (single geometry) and general (superposition of geometries) QRFs. It then delves into the mathematical details of constructing the invariant volume element on the general frame bundle $F(M)$.
why_interesting: While highly mathematical, the concept of a QRF is foundational for quantum gravity and quantum field theory in curved spacetime, making it relevant to theoretical physics concerned with spacetime structure.
